true: The reader broadly studies EMBODIED INTELLIGENCE OR WORLD MODELS. Either area is sufficient; a paper does not need to combine both, mention a particular keyword, or focus on evaluation or acceleration. Include work whose substantive contribution concerns: (1) embodied agents and robotics, including robot learning, VLA and generalist/foundation robot policies with or without world models, imitation and reinforcement learning for embodied tasks, manipulation and dexterous hands, locomotion and humanoids, navigation and mobile manipulation, embodied reasoning and planning, language grounding, memory, human-robot interaction, tactile/multimodal sensing, and perception, mapping, geometry or spatial/scene understanding explicitly designed or evaluated for embodied agents; (2) learned world models, environment/dynamics/action models, predictive representations such as JEPA, latent actions and latent dynamics, interactive or action-conditioned video/world generation, learned physical simulators, and model-based control or planning in real, simulated, virtual or game environments, even without a robotics application; (3) supporting contributions directly connected to either area: robot demonstrations and data collection, synthetic interaction data, embodied datasets, simulation and digital twins, sim-to-real transfer, robot systems/hardware or sensors enabling embodied capabilities, evaluation and benchmarks, generalization, robustness and safety, interpretability, efficiency, acceleration and deployment. Include embodied perception even without prediction or control; include robot policies even without a world model. Judge relevance from the actual task, method and evaluation in the title and abstract rather than exact keywords.
false: The paper is outside BOTH embodied intelligence AND world models, and has no substantive contribution to either. Examples include generic NLP, speech, code generation, web/GUI-only agents, networks or communications, image restoration, static 3D reconstruction, or artistic image/video generation without an embodied-agent, interactive-environment, predictive-world-model or learned-dynamics contribution. Generic reinforcement learning or generic VLM/LLM work alone is not sufficient when neither embodied tasks nor world modeling is studied. Incidental mentions of robots, physical intelligence, world models or possible future robotic applications are not sufficient. Do not reject a paper merely because it is perception-only, lacks a world model, is not about efficiency/evaluation, or uses a simulated/virtual environment: it is relevant whenever either of the two research areas is substantively addressed. Application domains such as autonomous driving, medical robotics and human-robot collaboration are relevant when the contribution concerns embodied intelligence or world modeling, rather than unrelated domain-specific analysis.
